targets.title: Comparative effectiveness of a complex care program for high-cost/high-need patients: a retrospective cohort study
targets.evidence_quote: In the matched samples, CCP patients had a significantly lower hazard of 180-day mortality compared with UPC in this replication cohort (0.71, 95% CI: 0.61–0.82). This was higher than the hazard ratio in the prior inception cohort (0.58, 95% CI: 0.47–0.70).
targets.outcome_quote: A reduced hazard of death was reproduced within a second incident cohort of among seriously ill adult patients who were empaneled to a CCP in an integrated health care system compared with matched, but unempaneled patients whose care remained within UPC.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors conclude the reduced mortality hazard recurred in a second incident cohort. Its smaller benefit does not override that positive verdict.
